question.text: The SEBI Act 1992, which is the parent statute under which SSE and SIA frameworks are notified, primarily empowers SEBI to:

answer.text: Regulate only commodity derivatives on recognised exchanges
Protect the interests of investors in securities, promote the development of and regulate the securities market
Supervise only insurance and pension products
Direct fiscal and monetary policy in coordination with RBI

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The Preamble and Section 11 of the SEBI Act 1992 empower SEBI to protect investors in securities, promote the development of the securities market, regulate intermediaries, prohibit fraudulent and unfair trade practices, and promote investor education — the umbrella under which SSE, SIA empanelment, and related regulations sit. **The Trap:** Commodity derivatives came under SEBI in 2015 (not the 1992 Act's primary focus). Insurance and pension sit under IRDAI/PFRDA. Monetary/fiscal policy is RBI/Govt domain. **Cross-Exam Context:** XII (Securities Markets Foundation) tests the broader SEBI Act scope; XXIII narrows to the SSE / SIA limb under the same statute. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When drafting your SIA cover-letter, cite SEBI Act Section 11(2)(b)-(c) alongside ICDR Reg 292K to anchor the statutory basis of your appointment — this helps in any later dispute about your authority to certify the SE's AIR.
